name: Baked hake in tomato, pepper and olive sauce
summary: Hake fillets baked in a smoky sauce of tomato, red and green peppers and olives until they just flake, served with lemon and steamed green beans.
about: Hake, caught in deep water off South Africa's west and south coasts, is sold fresh and frozen across the country. Baking it in a Mediterranean-style tomato, pepper and olive sauce keeps the mild, flaky fillets moist.
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Warm the olive oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium heat. Tip in the onion and both peppers, sprinkle with a pinch of the salt and let them soften for about 10 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until limp and lightly browned in places.
Stir in the garlic and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomatoes, water, olives, black pepper and most of the remaining salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to hold a line when you drag a spoon through it.

If your pan is not ovenproof, tip the sauce into a baking dish of about 30 × 20 cm. Pat the hake dry, season it with the last of the salt and nestle the fillets into the sauce, spooning a little over the edges.
Bake uncovered for 12–15 minutes, until the fish is white all the way through and flakes when pressed with a fork.
While the fish bakes, steam or boil the green beans for 5–6 minutes, until bright green and tender but still with a little bite. Drain.
Scatter the parsley over the fish and serve with the beans and lemon wedges for squeezing.
prepNote: Make the sauce up to 2 days ahead and chill it; reheat it until bubbling before adding the fish.
